topics.topic: Define the canonical total ordering of input and output port names
questions: What total order defines “name order” for ports: Unicode code-point order, UTF-8 byte order, locale-sensitive order, or another order, and is it applied independently to input and output ports?
Which total ordering of port names determines the stored and returned order, separately for inputs and outputs?
What comparison defines name order independently for the binding's input ports and output ports, including case and non-ASCII names?

quotes:
8. A proposal that passes every check of rule 5 but gives its input and output
   ports out of name order is recorded, and the answer is that one binding with
   its ports in name order; another proposal of the same operation already in
   the store is not the answer. A proposal failing a check of rule 5 is refused
   whatever its port order.
judgement.why: P1 judged the same ordering question on the same unchanged passages, and the change since closure does not postdate or alter that judgement.
options: Unicode code-point order, applied within the input and output port collections through the (direction, name) key
One combined ordering that does not preserve the input/output collections
consequences: Unicode code-point ordering places `Z` before `a` and `a10` before `a2`; the stored and returned OperationBinding exposes that deterministic order.

precedent.topic: Exact total ordering and scope for input and output port names
quotes: content_identity: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Before hashing, lists whose order carries no meaning MUST be sorted so that the same content in another order has the same identity: ports by (direction, name), flow nodes by node_id, flow edges by (to_node, to_port, from_node, from_port), flow constants by (to_node, to_port), all compared as text by Unicode code point; every other list keeps its order, in particular trial_case_ids of a corpus (corpus order is meaningful) and the elements of any JSON value.

record_change: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] A content record is written with its order-free lists in the order content_identity sorts them before hashing — ports by (direction, name), flow nodes by node_id, flow edges by (to_node, to_port, from_node, from_port), flow constants by (to_node, to_port) — never in the order a caller submitted them, so equal content submitted in another order is the same record with the same lists, and every read returns those lists in that order; an OperationBinding, a lifecycle record, writes its inputs and outputs the same way, ports by (direction, name), the name order A08 checks a proposal's ports in; every other list, and every JSON value, keeps its order.

propose_binding: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST return the one OperationBinding of the RecordSet record_change returns, which holds exactly the binding the ProposeBindingChange wrote, with status proposed and its ports in (direction, name) order; that record is returned as written and is never looked up again or matched against the proposal's ports, whose order the caller chose.
precedent.why: The State 8 notes define the relation as Unicode code-point comparison of the (direction, name) key and apply it to an OperationBinding's separate inputs and outputs when written and returned.
options: Unicode code-point order, applied within the input and output port collections through the (direction, name) key
One combined ordering that does not preserve the input/output collections
consequences: Unicode code-point ordering places `Z` before `a` and `a10` before `a2`; the stored and returned OperationBinding exposes that deterministic order.

topics.topic: Decide whether a refused binding proposal may be persisted
questions: Must refusal leave no OperationBinding record, or may a proposed binding be stored even though the action returns a refusal?

quotes: propose_binding: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise RefusedError naming the first failing check as a manifest mismatch, in this order: every check of read_manifest_operation; no instance selected; the selected instance missing from the record or its api_base_url missing or not an absolute http or https URL with a host; two required headers share a name compared without regard to case, or one is named in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant without being in the imported INSTANCE_SETTABLE_HEADER_NAMES constant; a required header whose name is not an HTTP field-name token, or whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character; for an effect class other than read, a key field that is not the name of a value carriage input port; check_request_shape answering fits false; port names repeating within a direction, a file port without exactly one media type or a value port with one; an input or output port without a disclosure class.

propose_binding: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] MUST write one ProposeBindingChange with the operation's record_digest pinned and the effect class and key fields copied from the manifest, never taken from the proposer, proposed_at from kernel_now and the given actor; record_change mints the binding_id.
judgement.why: The later notes require validation to raise RefusedError on the first failed check and specify the write only for the path that proceeds to ProposeBindingChange, so a refused proposal writes no OperationBinding.
options: Refuse but retain a proposed binding when enough fields are available to construct one
consequences: Under the decided option, later inspection finds no OperationBinding created by the refused proposal.
Persisting a proposed binding after RefusedError would contradict the later validation-before-write flow.
